newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops closer to rebel town - minister.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops closer to rebel town - minister.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops overcame stiff resistance from separatist Tamil Tiger guerrillas to edge closer to a rebel-held junction town in the island's north, the Defence Ministry said on Monday.
Troops, backed by artillery and tanks, on Sunday took the village of Periyamadu in the rebels' northern Wanni heartland, just south of the town of Puliyankulam , a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
"Our artillery and air attacks caused heavy casualties among the terrorists," the spokesman said.
A Defence Ministry statement said troops confirmed between 15 to 20 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels had been killed and more than 60 wounded in Sunday's fighting.
Five soldiers were killed while one officer and eight soldiers had been wounded, the statement added.
The LTTE's clandestine Voice of Tigers radio, monitored in Vavuniya, said army artillery shells had landed at Mankulam, about 40 km (25 miles) north of Puliyankulam, along the army's path of advance.
"At least 25 shells were fired at Mankulam on Sunday afternoon. Everything was demolished -- houses, buildings and shops," the radio said.
It said seven civilians were killed and at least 15 were wounded. Casualties would have been higher had the town's market been open, it added.
The military denied the rebels' report, saying it had only engaged identified rebel targets.
Independent confirmation of events is not possible as international media have not been allowed into the war zone.
Some 20,000 government troops are advancing on two flanks into the mostly shrub-covered rebel stronghold.

The army captured the towns of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya on one flank, and Nedunkeni, 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya on the other, in an offensive codenamed "Operation Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", launched on May 13.
Vavuniya is 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte said last week the offensive's aim was to open a land supply route to Jaffna, 100 km (60 miles) further north of Vavuniya, that would help rehabilitation work there.

The north-south highway has been closed for more than 10 years due to the war which began in 1983. The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the fighting began. The rebels say the toll is higher.
